narrative.text: Above-normal rainfall is likely across most of the region, with the highest probabilities over north-eastern Kenya, central to southern Somalia and south-eastern Ethiopia.
Across much of the remaining region, the probability of above-normal rainfall is generally in the range of 50–70%.

sources.label: Kiremt 2026 Assessment and Bega 2026_27 Outlook Hydro met Bulletin

narrative.text: October: Humid to wet conditions across southern and southwestern catchments Baro-Akobo, Wabi Shebelle, Genale Dawa, Ogaden, and Abay support initial surface water accumulation.
November: Moisture shifts southward; wet to very wet conditions continue in Genale Dawa, Wabi Shebelle, Baro- Akobo, Ogaden, and parts of Abay Rift Valley, while northern areas dry out.

December: Dry to arid conditions dominate northern, central, and eastern basins Afar-Denakil, Aysha, middle upper Abay, Tekeze, and Awash. Sub-humid to wet levels persist in Omo-Gibe, Rift Valley, Baro-Akobo, Genale Dawa, Wabi Shebelle, and middle lower Ogaden.
January: Arid conditions expand across most northern, central, and eastern catchments. Sub-humid to wet conditions remain confined to Omo-Gibe, Rift Valley, and upper Genale Dawa.

paragraphs.text: The platform favours below-normal rainfall in the area EMI's arrow marks for zone III, while the EMI outlook favours above-normal rainfall. This indicates disagreement in the favoured rainfall category. EMI prints below / near / above 20% / 25% / 55% for the zone; the platform's area mean of local probabilities within ±0.5° of the arrow tip is 50% / 31% / 19%. An exact zone probability difference has not been calculated because the zone boundary is not published with the figure (only an arrow locates it) and the EMI reference period is not stated.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions in the area EMI's arrow marks for zone VI. EMI prints below / near / above 15% / 25% / 60% for the zone; the platform's area mean of local probabilities within ±0.5° of the arrow tip is 22% / 24% / 55%. An exact zone probability difference has not been calculated because the zone boundary is not published with the figure (only an arrow locates it) and the EMI reference period is not stated.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions in the area EMI's arrow marks for zone VII. EMI prints below / near / above 25% / 15% / 60% for the zone; the platform's area mean of local probabilities within ±0.5° of the arrow tip is 24% / 21% / 55%. An exact zone probability difference has not been calculated because the zone boundary is not published with the figure (only an arrow locates it) and the EMI reference period is not stated.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions in the area EMI's arrow marks for zone VIII. EMI prints below / near / above 10% / 15% / 75% for the zone; the platform's area mean of local probabilities within ±0.5° of the arrow tip is 19% / 24% / 57%. An exact zone probability difference has not been calculated because the zone boundary is not published with the figure (only an arrow locates it) and the EMI reference period is not stated.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions in the part of Ethiopia where both show a favoured category. Over Ethiopia, the ICPAC map shows a favoured category on 46% of the area (54% is grey, without a forecast); it favours above normal on 100% of that, most often at 70-80% above-normal and 80-90% above-normal. The platform favours above normal on 71% and below normal on 17% of the area. Where both show a favoured category (45% of the area), the categories agree on 94% and are opposite (above vs below) on 5%. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so the platform's probabilities are not differenced against it. The target periods differ: the official outlook covers Oct 2026–Dec 2026 and the platform Oct 2026–Jan 2027 (only in the platform: Jan 2027; only in the official outlook: none). This compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions in the part of the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain where both show a favoured category. Over the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain, the ICPAC map shows a favoured category on 100% of the area (0% is grey, without a forecast); it favours above normal on 100% of that, most often at 70-80% above-normal and 80-90% above-normal. The platform favours above normal on 100% and below normal on 0% of the area. Where both show a favoured category (100% of the area), the categories agree on 100% and are opposite (above vs below) on 0%. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so the platform's probabilities are not differenced against it. The target periods differ: the official outlook covers Oct 2026–Dec 2026 and the platform Oct 2026–Jan 2027 (only in the platform: Jan 2027; only in the official outlook: none). This compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Not calculated: rainfall-anomaly differences, because no official rainfall-amount anomaly product was found in the checked ICPAC and EMI products; which forecast is more accurate, because that needs observations and a separate verification design (see Verification); zone-mean platform probabilities for EMI zones, because the zone boundaries are not published with the figure; same-event probability differences, because the target windows or spatial supports differ and ICPAC publishes only favoured-category intervals.

notes: Area means are area-weighted means of local grid-cell probabilities, not probabilities of area-mean rainfall.
Favoured category: the leading tercile where it reaches 40% (the map display rule); otherwise no clear category.
An OND probability cannot be built by averaging monthly probabilities; ONDJ and OND are compared only as spatial tendencies.
